Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 1–6:

The explanation of the words of God Most High: ﴿By those sent forth in gusts (ʿurfan), (1) and those that rage in violence (ʿasfan), (2) and those that scatter (nashran), (3) and those that separate (farqan), (4) and those that deliver a message (dhikran), (5) as an excuse or a warning (ʿudhran aw nudhran), (6)﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of God's words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "By the winds that are sent, one following another." They said: "al-mursalat" are the winds.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, and he said: "The wind."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related to us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, that he asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he mentioned something similar.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud," and he mentioned something similar.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, meaning: "The wind."

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Muʿadh related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Shuʿba, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, the companion of al-Kalbi, regarding His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, who said: "They are the winds."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, who said: "The wind."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah concerning ﴿al-mursalati ʿurfan﴾," and he said: "The wind."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, who said: "They are the wind."

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "By the angels who are sent with ʿurf (goodness/kindness)."

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, who said: "Masruq used to say concerning al-mursalat: they are the angels."

- Isra'il ibn Abi Isra'il related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Sulayman, who said: "I heard Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾," who said: "The angels."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh and Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾, who said: "They are the messengers sent with ʿurf."

- ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Isma'il, who said: "I asked Abu Salih concerning His words: ﴿wal-mursalati ʿurfan﴾," and he said: "They are the messengers sent with what is known (al-ma'ruf)." They said: "So the meaning of the statement is: 'And the angels who were sent by the command of God and His prohibition, and that is the ʿurf."

Others said: what is meant by His words ﴿ʿurfan﴾ is "successive, like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse," as the Arabs say: "The people are to so-and-so one mane," when they head towards him in large numbers.

Mention of those who said that:

- It was related to me from Dawud ibn al-Zibriqan, from Salih ibn Buraydah, regarding His words: ﴿ʿurfan﴾, who said: "One follows another."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is to say: God, dhikruhu, swore by "those sent forth in ʿurf." Both the angels and the winds are sent in ʿurf, and there is no indication that shows that what is meant is one of the two groups to the exclusion of the other. God, may His praise be exalted, has made His oath general over everything whose attribute is what He described. So whoever has that attribute is included in His oath: an angel, a wind, or a human messenger who is sent.

* *

His words: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾

Exalted is His remembrance: "By the winds that rage in violence (ʿasfan)," meaning: those that blow intensely and pass swiftly.

The interpreters said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from Khalid, from ʿUrʿura, that a man stood up before ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, and said: "What are al-ʿasifat ʿasfan?" He said: "The wind."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, that he asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "What are al-ʿasifat ʿasfan?" He said: "The wind."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud," and he mentioned the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah," and he mentioned the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, "The wind."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, who said: "They are the winds."

- ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, who said: "I asked Abu Salih concerning His words: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾," and he said: "They are the winds."

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Shu'ba, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, the companion of al-Kalbi, regarding His words: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, who said: "They are the winds."

- Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya al-Darir and Sa'id ibn Muhammad related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, who said: "It is the wind."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, the like of it.

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿUrʿura, from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, who said: "The wind."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿fal-ʿasifati ʿasfan﴾, who said: "The winds."

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

* *

His words: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: what is meant by al-nashirat nashran is: the wind.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud concerning ﴿al-nashirati nashran﴾, and he said: "The wind."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of it.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud," and he mentioned the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: "I asked ʿAbd Allah," and he mentioned the like of it.

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾, who said: "The wind."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Shu'ba, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, the companion of al-Kalbi, regarding His words: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾, who said: "They are the winds."

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾, who said: "The winds."

Others said: they are the rain.

Mention of those who said that:

- ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Isma'il, who said: "I asked Abu Salih concerning His words: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾," and he said: "The rain."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾, who said: "They are the rain."

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, the like of it.

Others said: rather, they are the angels who spread the books.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ahmad ibn Hisham related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih: ﴿wal-nashirati nashran﴾, who said: "The angels who spread the books."

The most correct of these views in our opinion is to say: God, dhikruhu, swore by "those that spread (nashran)," and did not specify any one of them over another. The wind spreads the clouds, the rain spreads the earth, and the angels spread the books. There is no indication, in any way that must be accepted, that what is meant is some and not others. So it applies to everything that spreads.

* *

His words: ﴿fal-farriqati farqan﴾

The interpreters differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: what is meant by that is: the angels who separate between truth and falsehood.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿fal-farriqati farqan﴾, who said: "The angels."

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿fal-farriqati farqan﴾, who said: "The angels."

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿fal-farriqati farqan﴾, who said: "The angels."

Others said: rather, what is meant by it is the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿fal-farriqati farqan﴾, meaning the Qur'an, which God has used to separate between truth and falsehood.

The correct view on this matter is to say: our Lord, may His praise be exalted, swore by "those that separate (al-farriqat)," who are those that make a distinction between truth and falsehood. He did not specify some of them over others, so it is an oath by everything that separates between truth and falsehood, whether an angel, the Qur'an, or other than that.

* *

His words: ﴿fal-mulqiyati dhikran﴾

He says: "By those who convey God's revelation to His messengers, and they are the angels."

The interpreters said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿fal-mulqiyati dhikran﴾, meaning: the angels.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿fal-mulqiyati dhikran﴾, who said: "They are the angels who cast the reminder upon the messengers and convey it."

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿fal-mulqiyati dhikran﴾, who said: "The angels who cast the Qur'an."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿fal-mulqiyati dhikran﴾, who said: "The angels."

* *

His words: ﴿ʿudhran aw nudhran﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "By those who cast the reminder to the messengers as an excuse (iʿdhar) from God to His creation, and as a warning (indhar) from Him to them."

The interpreters said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn ʿAbd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿ʿudhran aw nudhran﴾, who said: "An excuse from God, and a warning from Him to His creation."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿ʿudhran aw nudhran﴾: "An excuse for God against His creation, and a warning to the believers, that they may benefit from it and act upon it."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ʿudhran aw nudhran﴾, meaning: the angels.

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Syria, and some of the Meccan and some of the Kufan readers, recited ﴿ʿudhran﴾ with lightening (takhfif) and nudhran with emphasis (tathqil). The majority of the readers of Kufa and some of the Basran readers recited both with lightening. Others from the people of Basra recited both with emphasis. The lightened recitation is more pleasing to me, although I do not reject the soundness of the emphatic recitation, since both are verbal nouns (masadir) meaning iʿdhar (excusing) and indhar (warning).

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Syria, and some of the Meccan and some of the Kufan readers, recited ﴿ʿudhran﴾ with lightening (takhfif) and nudhran with emphasis (tathqil). The majority of the readers of Kufa and some of the Basran readers recited both with lightening. Others from the people of Basra recited both with emphasis. The lightened recitation is more pleasing to me, although I do not reject the soundness of the emphatic recitation, since both are verbal nouns (masadir) meaning iʿdhar (excusing) and indhar (warning).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 7–15:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised will surely occur. So when the stars are obliterated, and when the sky is split open, and when the mountains are blown away, and when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time. For what day were they postponed? For the Day of Decision. And what can make you know what is the Day of Decision? Woe, that Day, to the deniers.﴾

Its meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: By those [winds] sent forth in succession, what you, O people, are promised of matters is surely going to occur, and it is certain without doubt, meaning by that the Day of Resurrection, and what Allah has prepared for His creation on that day of reward and punishment.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾

He says: when the stars have their light removed, so that they have no radiance or brightness. ﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ means: when the sky is cleft and rent asunder. ﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾ means: when the mountains are blown away from their foundations, so that they become scattered dust. ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾ means, may His remembrance be exalted: when the messengers are gathered together for their appointed time on the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾: he said, "gathered."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿uqqitat﴾, he said: "ujjilat" (were postponed).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "postponed."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, both from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "were threatened" (uwʻidat).

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾: "They were appointed for the Day of Resurrection," and he recited: ﴿The Day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾, and said: "al-ajal" is "al-miqat" (the appointed time), and he recited: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: they are times for the people and for the Hajj﴾, and he recited: ﴿until a known appointed day﴾, and said: "until the Day of Resurrection; they have a term until that day, until they reach it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "were promised" (wu'idat).

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of Medina, other than Abu Ja'far, and the majority of the readers of Kufa, recited it: ﴿uqqitat﴾ with an alif and a doubled qaf. Some readers of Basra recited it with a waw and a doubled qaf: ﴿wuqqitat﴾. Abu Ja'far recited it: ﴿wuqitat﴾ with a waw and a single qaf.

The correct position on this is to say: all of these are well-known recitations and widely attested dialects with one meaning. Whichever of them the reader recites is correct. It is in fact the form fu'‌'‌‌ilat from the root "waqt" (time), except that some Arabs find the damma on the waw heavy, just as they find the kasra on the yā' at the beginning of a word heavy, so they make it a hamza, saying: "hadhihi ajwuhun hisan" with a hamza, and some of them recite:

yaḥullu ajīduhu wa-yuqālu baʻlun ... wa-mithlu tamawwulin minhu ifti-qār

[[A reference to what has passed: 146. In the originals here "al-'Arzami" also appears, with the zay placed first, which is an error, as we have explained before.]]

As for His saying: ﴿For what day were they postponed?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, amazing His servants at the terror and severity of that day: For what day were the messengers postponed and appointed? How great and how terrible it is. Then He explains it: what day is it? He said: they were postponed ﴿for the Day of Decision﴾, meaning: for the day on which Allah decides between His creatures with judgment, takes for the wronged from the wrongdoer, and rewards the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿For what day were they postponed? For the Day of Decision﴾: the day on which people are separated by their deeds, to Paradise and to Hell.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what is the Day of Decision?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And what can make you know, O Muhammad, what the Day of Decision is, magnifying its affair and the severity of its terror.

As follows:

⁕ Bishr related to me, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And what can make you know what is the Day of Decision?﴾, glorifying that day.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the valley that flows in Hell with the pus of its people is for those who deny the Day of Decision.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾: "Woe, by Allah, is long."

So when the stars are obliterated, and when the sky is split open, and when the mountains are blown away, and when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time. For what day were they postponed? For the Day of Decision. And what can make you know what is the Day of Decision? Woe, that Day, to the deniers.﴾

Its meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: By those [winds] sent forth in succession, what you, O people, are promised of matters is surely going to occur, and it is certain without doubt, meaning by that the Day of Resurrection, and what Allah has prepared for His creation on that day of reward and punishment.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the stars are obliterated﴾

He says: when the stars have their light removed, so that they have no radiance or brightness. ﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ means: when the sky is cleft and rent asunder. ﴿And when the mountains are blown away﴾ means: when the mountains are blown away from their foundations, so that they become scattered dust. ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾ means, may His remembrance be exalted: when the messengers are gathered together for their appointed time on the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾: he said, "gathered."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿uqqitat﴾, he said: "ujjilat" (were postponed).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: Mujahid said: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "postponed."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, both from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "were threatened" (uwʻidat).

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾: "They were appointed for the Day of Resurrection," and he recited: ﴿The Day when Allah gathers the messengers﴾, and said: "al-ajal" is "al-miqat" (the appointed time), and he recited: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: they are times for the people and for the Hajj﴾, and he recited: ﴿until a known appointed day﴾, and said: "until the Day of Resurrection; they have a term until that day, until they reach it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the messengers are gathered to their appointed time﴾, he said: "were promised" (wu'idat).

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples? (16) Then We shall follow them with the later ones. (17) Thus do We deal with the criminals. (18) Woe on that day to the deniers. (19)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Did We not destroy the earlier nations who denied Our messengers and rejected Our signs, such as the people of Noah, ʿAad and Thamud? Then We follow them with the later ones after them, those who trod their path in disbelief in Me and in My messenger, such as the people of Ibrahim, the people of Lut, and the companions of Madyan. So We destroy them just as We destroyed the earlier ones before them. ﴿Thus do We deal with the criminals﴾ means: just as We destroyed these people for their disbelief in Me and their denial of My messengers, so is My custom with their like among the disbelieving nations; We destroy the criminals for their crimes when they transgress and oppress. ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ means: to those who deny the reports of God mentioned in this verse, who reject His power to do whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 25–28:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ [25] ﴿for the living and the dead?﴾ [26] ﴿And We placed therein firm mountains high (rising), and gave you to drink sweet water.﴾ [27] ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ [28]

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, admonishing His servants concerning His blessings upon them: ﴿Have We not made﴾ O people ﴿the earth﴾ for you ﴿a receptacle (kifatan)﴾, meaning: a vessel. It is said: "This is the kifat of this, and I gathered it (kafaytu-hu)," when it is its container.

The meaning of the speech is: Have We not made the earth a receptacle for your living and your dead, gathering your living in the dwellings and houses, embracing and collecting them therein, and your dead in its bellies, in the graves, where they are buried therein.

It is also permissible that what is intended by His saying ﴿a receptacle for the living and the dead﴾ is that it gathers their filth during their lives and their carcasses after their deaths.

The exegetes stated what is similar to what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾: he said: a shelter (kinnan).

- Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Khalid informed us, from Muslim, from Zadhan Abu Umar, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he found a louse in his garment, so he buried it in the mosque, then said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, he said: Muslim al-A'war related to us, from Zadhan, from Rabi ibn Khuthaym, from Abdullah, the like of it.

- Ya'qub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, he said: Mujahid said, concerning one who sees a louse in his garment while he is in the mosque, and I do not know whether he said in prayer or not: if you wish, throw it away, and if you wish, bury it, ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki related to us, from Shurayk, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾ He said: its belly is for your dead, and its back is for your living.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ He said: it gathers their filth. ﴿Living﴾: it conceals them. ﴿And dead﴾: they are buried; it gathers them.

- Ibn Humayd related this to me another time, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ He said: it gathers their filth and what comes out of them. ﴿Living and dead﴾ He said: it gathers them among the living and the dead.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾ He said: living, they dwell in it. Muhammad ibn Amr said: they are hidden in it as they wish. And al-Harith said: and they are hidden in it as they wish.

* *

As for His saying ﴿living and dead﴾

He said: they are buried therein.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾ Their living dwell in it, and their dead are buried in it.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿living and dead﴾ He said: living, upon it on its back; and dead, who are buried in it.

The grammarians differed concerning what put ﴿living and dead﴾ in the accusative. Some grammarians of Basra said: it is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). And this view is more similar to the truth in my opinion.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 25–28:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ [25] ﴿for the living and the dead?﴾ [26] ﴿And We placed therein firm mountains high (rising), and gave you to drink sweet water.﴾ [27] ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ [28]

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, admonishing His servants concerning His blessings upon them: ﴿Have We not made﴾ O people ﴿the earth﴾ for you ﴿a receptacle (kifatan)﴾, meaning: a vessel. It is said: "This is the kifat of this, and I gathered it (kafaytu-hu)," when it is its container.

The meaning of the speech is: Have We not made the earth a receptacle for your living and your dead, gathering your living in the dwellings and houses, embracing and collecting them therein, and your dead in its bellies, in the graves, where they are buried therein.

It is also permissible that what is intended by His saying ﴿a receptacle for the living and the dead﴾ is that it gathers their filth during their lives and their carcasses after their deaths.

The exegetes stated what is similar to what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾: he said: a shelter (kinnan).

- Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Khalid informed us, from Muslim, from Zadhan Abu Umar, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he found a louse in his garment, so he buried it in the mosque, then said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, he said: Muslim al-A'war related to us, from Zadhan, from Rabi ibn Khuthaym, from Abdullah, the like of it.

- Ya'qub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, he said: Mujahid said, concerning one who sees a louse in his garment while he is in the mosque, and I do not know whether he said in prayer or not: if you wish, throw it away, and if you wish, bury it, ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki related to us, from Shurayk, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾ He said: its belly is for your dead, and its back is for your living.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ He said: it gathers their filth. ﴿Living﴾: it conceals them. ﴿And dead﴾: they are buried; it gathers them.

- Ibn Humayd related this to me another time, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle﴾ He said: it gathers their filth and what comes out of them. ﴿Living and dead﴾ He said: it gathers them among the living and the dead.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle for the living and the dead?﴾ He said: living, they dwell in it. Muhammad ibn Amr said: they are hidden in it as they wish. And al-Harith said: and they are hidden in it as they wish.

* *

As for His saying ﴿living and dead﴾

He said: they are buried therein.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Set off toward that which you used to deny﴾ (29) ﴿Set off toward a shadow of three branches﴾ (30) ﴿Neither shady nor sufficient against the blaze﴾ (31) ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾ (32) ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾ (33) ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers!﴾ (34)

He, exalted is His mention, says to those who denied these blessings and the proofs with which He argued against them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Set off toward that which you used to deny﴾ in the world, ﴿you used to deny﴾ concerning the punishment of God for the people of disbelief in Him. ﴿Set off toward a shadow of three branches﴾: He, exalted is His mention, means: toward the shadow of smoke with three branches, ﴿neither shady﴾. That is because the smoke rises from its fuel, it is said, and when it ascends it divides into three branches, and this is His saying: ﴿of three branches﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿toward a shadow of three branches﴾, he said: the smoke of Hell.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿a shadow of three branches﴾, he said: It is like His saying: ﴿a fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾. He said: The enclosure (suradiq) is the smoke of the fire, which surrounds them, then it divides and becomes three branches. So He said: Set off toward a shadow of three branches: one branch here, one branch here, and one branch here. ﴿Neither shady nor sufficient against the blaze﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Neither shady﴾

He says: it does not shade them from its heat, ﴿nor is it sufficient against the blaze﴾, nor does it shelter them from its flame.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed Hell throws up sparks like a fortress. The readers of the metropolitan cities recited ﴿kalqasr﴾ with the sād unvowelled (sukūn).

Those who recited it thus differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: it is the singular of "qusur" (palaces).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, he said: like a great palace.

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, he said: mention of the fortress [[The people of ignorance in our age still write it, and boast of mentioning it in their lectures and books, quoting those who gather what has fallen from sayings, namely the non-Arabs who compose on matters they do not understand, under the name of Orientalism. Al-Tabari's refutation is decisive for whoever has, from ignorance and error, a refutation that prevents him from obstinacy.]].

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yazid ibn Yunus informed me, from Abu Sakhr, regarding the saying of God: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, he said: al-Qurazi used to say: Indeed over Hell there is a wall, and what emerges from behind the wall, which returns into it, is in the magnitude of a fortress and the colour of pitch.

Others said: rather, it is the thick wood, like the roots of palm trees and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Waki told us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, and he said: "al-Qasr" is wood which we used to store for winter, three cubits and more, and less than that we would call "al-qasr".

⁕ Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Mu'ammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis say: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾: "al-Qasr" is wood that used to be cut in the Jahiliyyah, a cubit or less or more, with which one builds.

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾: In the Jahiliyyah we used to cut two or three cubits, and more than that and less than that we would call "al-qasr".

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾: "al-Qasr" is cut trees; it is said: "al-qasr" is cut palm trees.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿like a fortress﴾, he said: a bundle of trees, meaning a bundle.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, he said: like the trunk of a palm tree.

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾: the roots of trees and the roots of palm trees.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿like a fortress﴾, he said: like the root of a tree.

⁕ I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿sparks like a fortress﴾: "al-Qasr" is the great roots of trees, as if they were the yellow camels' marrow-bones, the middle of everything being its marrow, and these are the marrow-bones.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, who said: al-Hasan recited it: ﴿kalqasr﴾ and said: it is the dry firewood. He said: its singular is "qasrah" and "qasr", like it: "jamrah" and "jamr", and "tamrah" and "tamr".

It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he recited it ﴿kalqasar﴾ with the sād vowelled (fatḥah).

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, who said: Husayn al-Mu'allim informed me, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he recited it ﴿kalqasar﴾ with the qaf and the sād both vowelled.

He said: Harun said: Abu Umar informed me that Ibn Abbas recited it ﴿kalqasar﴾ and said: "qasr al-nakhl", meaning the necks.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is that of the metropolitan readers, namely the unvowelled sād. The most correct interpretation of it is that it is "al-qusur" (palaces), as is shown by the evidence of His saying: ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾. The Arabs liken camels to built palaces, as al-Akhtal said describing a she-camel:

As if she were a Roman tower that was built,
Bound with plaster, brick and stones [[I have not found the speaker of this verse. Ibn Sidah cited it in al-Mukhassas 17:152. Muhammad Mahmud al-Turkuzi al-Shinqiti commented on the verse, claiming it is fabricated, and that "some men who love to produce non-existent evidence for their bare claims made it up and fabricated it, and its fabrication and artifice are evident as the sun at mid-morning, and its weakness proclaims aloud its fabricated nature. The correct view, which is the agreed truth, is that the pre-Islamic poet referred to is al-Shanfara al-Azdi, and this verse is not in his poetry," and that it is compiled from al-Shanfara's saying: "Would that I knew, though regret is misguided, what the girl's hand struck of her camel." Al-Shinqiti, may God have mercy on him, was much given to self-exaltation and quick to boast of his learning and narration. What he said about fabrication does not stand. The verse that follows it suffices as proof of the falsity of his claim that the motive for its fabrication is producing non-existent evidence for bare claims. There is neither weakness nor artifice in the verse.]]

It is also said: ﴿like a fortress﴾ and not "like palaces" — and "sparks" is a collective noun, as it is said: ﴿The host will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾, and it does not say "backs", because "dubur" means "adbar". This is done to harmonize the endings of verses and the pauses of speech, for the Arabs do this, and the Qur'an was revealed in their tongue. It is also said: "like a fortress", meaning "like the magnitude of a fortress", as it is said: ﴿Their eyes roll like one who is overcome by death﴾, and it does not say "like the eyes of one overcome", because what is intended in the comparison is the action, not the eye.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, that he asked al-Aswad about this verse: ﴿it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾, and he said: like a fortress.

* *

And His saying: ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning is: as if the sparks which Hell throws up like a fortress were black she-camels, that is, black female camels. They said: "yellow" in this place means black. They said: it is only called "yellow" while being black because the colours of camels are black tending toward yellowness, and for this reason they are called "yellow", just as gazelles are called "adam" because of the darkness that overlays their whiteness.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Amr al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar told us, saying: Abbad ibn Rashid told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Hasan, ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾, he said: black female camels.

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾: like the black she-camels you have seen.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿yellow camels﴾, he said: black she-camels.

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us; and Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki told us, both from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾, he said: they are camels.

⁕ He said: Mihran told us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾, he said: like the black she-camels you have seen.

Others said: rather, what is meant is the ropes of ships, with which the sparks were compared.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾: the yellow camels are the ship's mooring-ropes, which are gathered and fastened with them.

And His saying: ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning is: as if the sparks which Hell throws up like a fortress were black she-camels, that is, black female camels. They said: it is only called "yellow" while being black because the colours of camels are black tending toward yellowness, and for this reason they are called "yellow", just as gazelles are called "adam" because of the darkness that overlays their whiteness.

The most correct of the sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: what is meant by "yellow camels" is black camels, because that is the well-known usage of the Arabs, and because "jimalat" is the plural of "jimal", like "rijal" and "rijalat", and "buyut" and "buyutat".

The readers have differed in reciting it. The readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufans, the common reading, recited ﴿jimalatun﴾ with a kasrah on the jim and the taʾ, as the plural of "jimal". It may also be that what is intended is the plural of "jimalah", and "jimalah" is the plural of "jamal", just as "hijarah" is the plural of "hajar", and "dhikarah" is the plural of "dhakar". The common reading of the Kufan readers was ﴿kaannahu jimalatun﴾ with a kasrah on the jim, as the plural of "jamal", pluralized as "jimalah", just as I mentioned for the plural of "hajar" as "hijarah". It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite ﴿jumalatun﴾ with the taʾ and a ḍammah on the jim, as if it were the plural of "jumalah" from "al-shay' al-mujmal" (the gathered thing).

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from al-Husayn al-Mu'allim, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

The correct view on this matter is that the reciter may choose whichever of the two readings he wishes: with a kasrah on the jim and the taʾ, or with a kasrah on the jim and the hāʾ which becomes taʾ in continuous reading, since these are the two well-known readings among the readers of the metropolitan cities. As for a ḍammah on the jim, I do not permit it, because the consensus of the authorities among the readers is against it.

And His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers!﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Woe on the Day of Resurrection to the deniers, this threat with which God has threatened the deniers among His servants.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Set off toward that which you used to deny﴾ (29) ﴿Set off toward a shadow of three branches﴾ (30) ﴿Neither shady nor sufficient against the blaze﴾ (31) ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like a fortress﴾ (32) ﴿As if they were yellow camels﴾ (33) ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers!﴾ (34)

He, exalted is His mention, says to those who denied these blessings and the proofs with which He argued against them on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Set off toward that which you used to deny﴾ in the world, ﴿you used to deny﴾ concerning the punishment of God for the people of disbelief in Him. ﴿Set off toward a shadow of three branches﴾: He, exalted is His mention, means: toward the shadow of smoke with three branches, ﴿neither shady﴾. That is because the smoke rises from its fuel, it is said, and when it ascends it divides into three branches, and this is His saying: ﴿of three branches﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿toward a shadow of three branches﴾, he said: the smoke of Hell.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿a shadow of three branches﴾, he said: It is like His saying: ﴿a fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾. He said: The enclosure (suradiq) is the smoke of the fire, which surrounds them, then it divides and becomes three branches. So He said: Set off toward a shadow of three branches: one branch here, one branch here, and one branch here. ﴿Neither shady nor sufficient against the blaze﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Neither shady﴾

He says: it does not shade them from its heat, ﴿nor is it sufficient against the blaze﴾, nor does it shelter them from its flame.

The most correct of the sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: what is meant by "yellow camels" is black camels, because that is the well-known usage of the Arabs, and because "jimalat" is the plural of "jimal", like "rijal" and "rijalat", and "buyut" and "buyutat".

The readers have differed in reciting it. The readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufans, the common reading, recited ﴿jimalatun﴾ with a kasrah on the jim and the taʾ, as the plural of "jimal". It may also be that what is intended is the plural of "jimalah", and "jimalah" is the plural of "jamal", just as "hijarah" is the plural of "hajar", and "dhikarah" is the plural of "dhakar". The common reading of the Kufan readers was ﴿kaannahu jimalatun﴾ with a kasrah on the jim, as the plural of "jamal", pluralized as "jimalah", just as I mentioned for the plural of "hajar" as "hijarah". It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite ﴿jumalatun﴾ with the taʾ and a ḍammah on the jim, as if it were the plural of "jumalah" from "al-shay' al-mujmal" (the gathered thing).

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf told us, saying: al-Qasim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from al-Husayn al-Mu'allim, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

The correct view on this matter is that the reciter may choose whichever of the two readings he wishes: with a kasrah on the jim and the taʾ, or with a kasrah on the jim and the hāʾ which becomes taʾ in continuous reading, since these are the two well-known readings among the readers of the metropolitan cities. As for a ḍammah on the jim, I do not permit it, because the consensus of the authorities among the readers is against it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers!﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Woe on the Day of Resurrection to the deniers, this threat with which God has threatened the deniers among His servants.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 35–40:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to offer an excuse﴾ (35–36). ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ (37). ﴿This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾ (38). ﴿So if you have any scheme, then scheme against Me!﴾ (39). ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾ (40).

He, may He be exalted, says to those who deny the reward and punishment of God: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾, meaning the people of denial of God's reward and punishment, ﴿nor will they be permitted to offer an excuse﴾ for the sins they committed in the world.

If someone says: How can it be said, ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾, when you know from God's report about them that they say: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out from it﴾ [23:107], and that they say: ﴿Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice﴾ [40:11], and similar things which God and His Messenger reported that they say? It is said: That applies in some situations and not others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾

It informs that they will not speak during some of the circumstances of that Day, not that they will not speak during the whole of that Day.

If it is said: Is there any proof by which the reality of that is known? It is said: Yes, and that is the attribution of "day" to the clause ﴿they will not speak﴾. The Arabs do not attribute "day" to a verb that is performed, except when they mean by the day an hour and a time within it. This is like their saying: "I will come to you on the day Such-and-such arrives," and "I came to you on the day your brother visited you." It is known that the meaning of that is: "I came to you at the hour of his visit," or "I will come at the hour of his arrival," and that his coming to him was not for the whole day, for had it been the entire day, "day" would not have been attributed to a verb in the perfect or imperfect. Rather, that is done because "day" here carries the sense of "idh" and "idha," which take verbs rather than nouns.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿so they make excuses﴾ (fa-ya'taziruna)

It is in the nominative (raf'), coordinated with His saying: ﴿nor will they be permitted﴾. This form was chosen over the accusative, though a negation precedes it, because it is the end of a verse (ra's ayah), and it is paired with the other verse-endings before it. Had it come in the accusative, it would have been permissible, as in His saying: ﴿nor will it be decreed for them so that they die﴾ [35:36]. Both are permissible in this, namely the nominative and the accusative, as was said of: ﴿Who is it that will lend God a goodly loan, so that He multiplies it for him﴾ [2:245], in both the nominative and the accusative.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers!﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Woe on that Day to those who deny God's report about these people and what He will do to them on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is the Day of Decision; We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾

He, may He be exalted, says to those who deny the resurrection on the day they are raised: This is the Day of Decision, on which God will judge between His servants with truth. (﴿We have gathered you and the former peoples﴾) meaning: We have gathered you on it for your appointed time which We promised you in the world; the gathering on it is between you and all who were before you of the destroyed nations. So We have fulfilled for you that promise. ﴿So if you have any scheme, then scheme against Me!﴾ meaning: God will surely carry out for you what He promised you in the world of punishment for your denial of Him and of your being raised for this Day. If you have any stratagem by which you can contrive to escape His punishment today, then devise it.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 77, verses 41–45:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among shades and springs (41) And fruit of whatever they desire. (42) "Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do." (43) Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. (44) Woe, that Day, to the deniers.﴾ (45)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who fear the punishment of God by performing His obligations in this world and avoiding His disobediences, ﴿among shades﴾, shades that are dense and sheltering, which do not let harm from heat or cold reach them, whereas the disbelievers in God are under a shade of three branches, which is neither dense nor protects from the flame. ﴿And springs﴾, rivers flowing among the trees of their gardens. ﴿And fruit of whatever they desire﴾, they eat from it whenever they wish, without fearing its harm or the unpleasant consequence of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It will be said to them: Eat, O people, from this fruit, and drink from these springs whenever you wish, with satisfaction; that is, there is no turbidity upon you, and no disturbance in what you eat and drink from it. Rather, it is lasting for you, not ending, and wholesome, not bringing you harm in your bodies.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for what you used to do﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: It will be said to them: This is a recompense for what you used to do in the world of obedience to God, and of striving in that which brings you near to Him.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed, you are criminals﴾, he said: It is meant for the people of disbelief.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: Woe that Day to the deniers, who denied the report of God which He informed them of concerning what He will do to them in this verse.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: And when it is said to these criminal deniers, who deny the warning of God, the people of denial of it: "Bow down," they do not bow down.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the time at which it is said to them. Some of them said: It is said to them on the Day of Judgment, when they are called to prostration, but they are unable to do it.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾, he said: They will be called on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, but they will be unable to prostrate, because they did not used to prostrate to God in the world.

Others said: Rather, it was said to them in the world.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾: "Upon you is good bowing, for prayer has a place with God." Qatadah also related from Ibn Mas'ud that he saw a man praying without bowing, and another dragging his waist-wrapper, and he laughed. They said: What makes you laugh? He said: Two men made me laugh. As for one of them, God does not accept his prayer; and as for the other, God does not look at him.

It was also said: By "bowing" in this place is meant the prayer.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Bow down," they do not bow down﴾, he said: They prayed.

The most preferable of these views regarding this is to say: this is a report from God, exalted is His remembrance, about these criminal people, that they were opposed to Him in His command and prohibition, not complying with His command and not refraining from what He forbade them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾

Says He: Woe to those who denied the messengers of God, and rejected what they conveyed to them of God's command and His prohibition for them.

* *

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ (50)

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: So in what statement after this Qur'an will they believe, that is, you, O people, who denied it despite the clarity of its proof and the soundness of its evidences, that it is the truth from God, will you believe? Meaning: will you affirm it?

God, may His remembrance be exalted, only informed them that if they do not affirm these reports which He informed them of in this Qur'an, despite the soundness of its arguments in its reality, it will not be possible for them to acknowledge the reality of any report about what they have not witnessed and not seen with their own eyes, and that if they affirm something of what is hidden from them due to evidence established for it, they would be obligated to do likewise regarding the reports of this Qur'an, and God knows best.

End of the commentary on Surat al-Mursalat.
